bib.title: Batch Normalization: Accelerating Deep Network Training by Reducing Internal Covariate Shift

question: Can normalizing layer inputs per mini-batch, as part of the architecture, reduce internal covariate shift and speed up and stabilise deep network training?
hypothesis: Fixing the means and variances of layer inputs reduces internal covariate shift and so accelerates training, permits higher learning rates, and regularizes.
contributions: Batch Normalizing Transform (Alg. 1) and its training/inference procedure (Alg. 2)
Extension to convolutional layers (normalize over batch and spatial locations, per feature map)
14x fewer training steps than the baseline Inception on ImageNet, and a better single network
Ensemble of BN networks at 4.9% top-5 validation error (4.82% test)

method.summary: Insert a per-feature normalization (mini-batch mean and variance, then learned scale gamma and shift beta) before each nonlinearity, backpropagating through the batch statistics. Tested on a 3-layer sigmoid MLP on MNIST and on a 13.6M-parameter Inception variant on ImageNet, with a set of training changes that BN allows.
method.task: image classification (MNIST digits; ImageNet LSVRC2012, 1000 classes)

datasets.name: MNIST
datasets.split: held-out test data used for accuracy; split sizes not stated

datasets.name: ImageNet LSVRC2012
datasets.split: trained on LSVRC2012 training data; validation set of 50000 images; test set of 100000 images via the ILSVRC server
datasets.preprocessing: photometric distortions reduced for BN models; within-shard shuffling enabled for BN-x5 and later

models.name: MNIST MLP
models.architecture: 3 fully-connected hidden layers of 100 sigmoid activations, then 10-way layer with cross-entropy

models.name: Inception (baseline)
models.architecture: GoogLeNet variant: 5x5 convs replaced by two 3x3 convs, 3 inception modules at 28x28, no fully-connected layers except softmax, separable conv depth multiplier 8 on first layer

models.name: BN-Baseline
models.architecture: Inception with BN before each nonlinearity

models.name: BN-x5-Sigmoid
models.architecture: Like BN-x5 with sigmoid instead of ReLU

training.optimizer: SGD with momentum (Sutskever et al., 2013); momentum value not stated
training.lr: Inception 0.0015; BN-x5 0.0075; BN-x30 0.045; BN-Baseline same as Inception
training.lr_schedule: Inception: exponential decay (rate not stated); BN variants decay 6 times faster
training.steps: MNIST 50000; ImageNet curves to about 30M steps; BN-x30 and ensemble members peak at about 6 · 10^6
training.weight_decay: L2 weight cut by a factor of 5 in BN models (base value not stated)
training.dropout: Inception 40%; BN-x5/x30 none; ensemble members 5% or 10%
training.regularisation: L2 loss; Local Response Normalization removed in BN models; photometric distortions reduced
training.hardware: large-scale distributed architecture similar to Dean et al., 2012; hardware not stated

other.bn_placement: immediately before the nonlinearity, applied to Wu with the bias dropped
other.conv_bn: effective mini-batch m' = m*p*q; gamma, beta per feature map
other.inference_stats: population mean and unbiased variance m/(m-1) * E_B[sigma_B^2]
other.ensemble_variation: increased initial conv weights; Dropout 5% or 10%; per-activation non-convolutional BN on last hidden layers

inference.samples: single run per model; no repeated runs reported

other.ensemble: 6 networks, arithmetic average of class probabilities
other.multicrop: 144 crops, details similar to Szegedy et al., 2014

metrics.name: validation accuracy @1
metrics.definition: probability of predicting the correct label out of 1000 on a held-out set, single crop per image

metrics.name: steps to 72.2%
metrics.definition: training steps to reach Inception's maximum accuracy

metrics.name: top-5 error
metrics.definition: ILSVRC top-5 error on validation set (50000) or test server (100000)

eval.protocol: Single run each; no seeds or variance; accuracy tracked as training progresses

evidence.quote: The model was trained using a version of Stochastic Gradient Descent with mo- mentum (Sutskever et al., 2013), using the mini-batch size of 32.

results.claim: BN-x5 reaches Inception's 72.2% accuracy in 14 times fewer steps.
results.setup: ImageNet LSVRC2012 single-crop validation accuracy @1, BN-x5 (BN + LR x5 + no Dropout + L2/5 + 6x faster decay + no LRN + more shuffling + fewer distortions) vs Inception, batch 32
results.quote: BN-x5 needs 14 times fewer steps than In- ception to reach the 72.2% accuracy.

results.claim: BN alone (BN-Baseline) matches Inception's accuracy in less than half the steps.
results.setup: ImageNet, BN-Baseline with the same learning rate as Inception, no other changes
results.quote: By only using Batch Normalization (BN-Baseline), we match the accuracy of Inception in less than half the num- ber of training steps.
results.table: Fig 3, row BN-Baseline, column Steps to 72.2%

results.claim: BN-x30 reaches a higher final accuracy than any other model.
results.quote: It reaches 74.8% after 6·106 steps, i.e. 5 times fewer steps than required by Inception to reach 72.2%.
results.table: Fig 3, row BN-x30, column Max accuracy
results.note: Fig 3 gives 2.7 · 10^6 steps to 72.2% for BN-x30

results.table: Fig 3, row BN-x5, column Max accuracy

results.claim: A 5x learning rate sent the original Inception's parameters to machine infinity.
results.setup: Inception without BN at initial LR 0.0075
results.quote: The same learning rate increase with original Inception caused the model pa- rameters to reach machine inﬁnity.

results.claim: A BN sigmoid network trains on ImageNet; Inception with sigmoid does not.
results.setup: ImageNet, BN-x5-Sigmoid vs Inception with sigmoid
results.quote: Indeed, BN-x5-Sigmoid achieves the accuracy of 69.8%.

results.claim: Ensemble of 6 BN-Inception networks gets 4.9% top-5 validation error and 4.82% test error.
results.setup: ImageNet, 6 networks based on BN-x30, 144 crops, validation set 50000 images
results.quote: Here we report a top-5 validation error of 4.9%, and test error of 4.82% (according to the ILSVRC server).
results.note: Abstract prints 4.8% test error; Sec 4.2.3 prints 4.82%

results.claim: Single BN-Inception model, single crop, top-5 error.
results.setup: ImageNet validation, 224 resolution, 1 crop, 1 model (top-1 error 25.2%)
results.table: Fig 4, row BN-Inception single crop, column Top-5 error

results.claim: Single BN-Inception model with 144 crops, top-5 error.
results.table: Fig 4, row BN-Inception multicrop, column Top-5 error

results.claim: BN trained MNIST sigmoid MLP to higher test accuracy and kept the input distribution to a sigmoid more stable.
results.setup: MNIST, 3x100 sigmoid MLP, 50000 steps, batch 60, one typical activation of last hidden layer, 15/50/85th percentiles
results.quote: The batch-normalized network enjoys the higher test accuracy.
results.note: No accuracy number printed; read from Fig 1a only

results.claim: More thorough within-shard shuffling gave about 1% validation accuracy gain.
results.setup: ImageNet BN-Inception; one of the bundled changes
results.quote: This led to about 1% improvements in the val- idation accuracy
results.note: No per-change ablation of the other changes

results.claim: Scale invariance: BN(Wu)=BN((aW)u), so gradient to W scales by 1/a.
results.setup: Analytical argument, Sec 3.3; the Jacobian singular-value claim is explicitly a conjecture
results.quote: We further conjecture that Batch Normalization may lead the layer Jacobians to have singular values close to 1

limits: Speedups come from a bundle of changes (LR x5, no Dropout, L2/5, faster decay, no LRN, shuffling, less distortion); only the BN-Baseline vs BN-x5 contrast exists, no per-change ablation.
Single runs, no seeds or variance; steps not wall-clock time.
The internal covariate shift explanation is shown on one activation of a small MNIST net; Jacobian claim is a conjecture ('remains an area of further study').
Momentum value, L2 weight, decay rate, epsilon, hardware and compute not stated; no code released.
Authors defer RNNs and domain adaptation to future work.
Later work questions the covariate-shift explanation (not in this source).

terms.definition: the change in the distribution of network activations due to the change in network parameters during training

code.snippet: mu_B = 1/m sum x_i; sigma2_B = 1/m sum (x_i - mu_B)^2; xhat_i = (x_i - mu_B)/sqrt(sigma2_B + eps); y_i = gamma*xhat_i + beta
